description: Somewhere in the vastness of the universe, there are questions we haven't thought to ask yet. We’re curious about what happens when we start looking.
summary:
For the NASA Space Apps Challenge, our team created Project Mandakini (SPHEREx Sky Viewer)—an interactive, browser-based tool designed to help anyone explore NASA's SPHEREx infrared mission data and hunt for moving celestial objects like Planet Nine, ultra-cool brown dwarfs, and variable stars.

Normally, analyzing multi-epoch astronomical FITS files requires specialized desktop software, command-line scripts, and steep learning curves. We wanted to make this data intuitive and immediately usable for both students and seasoned astronomers.

Our application connects directly to NASA’s Infrared Science Archive (IRSA), pulls multi-epoch cutouts across SPHEREx’s six spectral bands, and aligns them on a shared celestial grid. Through a responsive web interface, users can blink through observation dates like a digital flipbook, run pixel-level difference subtraction, co-add exposures to reveal faint targets hidden in detector noise, and click any pixel to plot light curves and spectra. By bringing research-grade analysis directly into the browser, Project Mandakini turns complex survey data into an open, accessible discovery playground.
details:
The system connects a lightweight scientific backend with a fast, interactive web client:

  1. Archive Ingestion & Alignment: When a user enters celestial coordinates (RA/Dec) or selects a preset target (like WISE 0855 or Barnard's Star), our Python backend queries NASA's IRSA TAP service. It retrieves SPHEREx Level 2 data across multiple observation epochs and spectral detectors (0.75 to 5.0 µm), performs WCS (World Coordinate System) alignment, masks bad detector pixels, and caches cutouts for instant repeat access.
    • Blink Sequence: Plays through multi-epoch frames in chronological order to highlight moving objects against static background stars.
    • Difference Imaging: Subtracts a baseline frame from subsequent epochs to produce distinct dipole signatures for moving or changing sources.
    • Stacking & Shift-and-Stack: Co-adds multiple frames to boost signal-to-noise ratio (∼N\sim\sqrt{N}∼N​), with adjustable proper-motion velocity sliders to track fast-moving cold objects.
    • Photometry & Spectra: Clicking on any pixel plots its flux history (light curve) across time and spectral distribution across SPHEREx’s detector bands.

Intended Impact & Benefits

  • Democratizing Astronomical Discovery: The search for hypothetical outer solar system bodies (like Planet Nine) and cold brown dwarfs requires sifting through vast sky surveys. Project Mandakini lowers the barrier to entry, letting school students, amateur astronomers, and citizen science communities participate in real discoveries without installing gigabytes of software.
  • Rapid Target Verification: Professional researchers can quickly verify candidate moving objects, check saturation flags, and evaluate multi-band infrared colors before scheduling time on major observatories like JWST.
  • Classroom & Public Engagement: With built-in presets, an all-sky contextual map (Aladin Lite), and visual explanations, the tool serves as an engaging educational platform for learning about infrared astronomy and time-domain science.

Tools & Tech Stack

  • Frontend: React 19, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, HTML5 Canvas API (for high-fps raw pixel rendering), and Lucide Icons.
  • Backend & Scientific Processing: Python 3, FastAPI, Uvicorn, Astropy (FITS handling, WCS reprojection, and TAP queries), NumPy, SciPy (aperture photometry and noise modeling), and Matplotlib (bicubic interpolation plots).
  • Data & Survey Services: NASA IPAC / IRSA (Infrared Science Archive) TAP service and Aladin Lite (for 2MASS, AllWISE, and DSS2 all-sky context).
  • Automation & Media: Playwright (headless Chrome automation for test recording) and FFmpeg.

What Makes Our Approach Creative

  • Everything Runs Live in the Browser: Instead of showing pre-rendered static GIFs, the canvas operates directly on calibrated physical flux numbers (MJy/sr), giving users true real-time contrast control and instant pixel inspection.
  • Smooth Bicubic Rendering with Data Integrity: Infrared detectors have coarse pixel scales. We implemented smooth bicubic interpolation for visual inspection without altering the underlying raw data used for photometric calculations.
  • Unified Discovery Workflow: In a single window, a user can search a target, view all-sky contextual surveys, compare six infrared wavelengths, subtract epochs to spot movement, and verify the object's spectrum. It bridges the gap between raw scientific data and visual storytelling.
